A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DrDiff research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison after matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original DrDiff benchmark results, component ablations, long-text stress tests, and timing measurements in Section 4 and the appendices, including Tables 1, 2, 5, 7, and 8.

after.justification: V2 retains the original DrDiff benchmark evaluations, ablations, stress tests, and timing results in the corresponding main-text and appendix tables and figures.

M1.justification: The HSA mechanism, expert routing, SAS targets and losses, and solver integration are unchanged. The abstract replaces 'soft absorption guidance optimization strategy' with 'Semantic Anchor States (SAS) module,' already described in v1 Section 3.4.

E1.justification: Both versions retain LongBench, the five-task evaluation in Table 2, Arxiv studies, and Gutenberg/PubMed/Wikipedia stress tests. Appendix A.9 describes the same training corpora; no evaluated task or domain is added.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in the corresponding benchmark and timing tables, including the GPT, Qwen, LLaMA, Longformer, and DiffuSeq comparisons. The dense/MoE comparison is also retained. Added citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Reported preprocessing, metrics, model configurations, and experimental budgets remain unchanged. Examples include the default 2048 diffusion steps in Table 3 and the 500-document, one-epoch SAS study in Appendix A.7.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same expert-count analysis, attention/window/step ablations, length stress tests, diffusion-schedule comparisons, SAS-weight study, and HSA/DES ablations. The corrected captions and references do not add analyses.

E5.justification: Table 2 retains standard-deviation reporting, and Appendix A.7 retains three-run averaging with a fixed seed and five generations per document. V1's linked '6' after 'random seed' becomes 'see Figure 6'; this clarifies a figure reference rather than changing the seed.

E6.justification: All numerical table entries and plotted results match. DrDiff remains at 33.5% overall on LongBench in Table 1 and 82.1 ± 0.6 TriviaQA F1 in Table 2. Appendix ablation, stress-test, sensitivity, and timing results are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10 and Appendix A.2's attention definitions, mode-selection rule, complexity derivations, and formal assertions are retained. Equation placement and typography change without altering the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and efficiency, coherence, and performance claims. Naming SAS consistently in the abstract does not introduce a contribution beyond the semantic-anchor mechanism already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: Interpretations of expert-count trade-offs, length degradation, diffusion schedules, and SAS quality/diversity effects remain unchanged. Both versions retain the same limitations concerning extreme lengths, theory, interpretability, memory overhead, and domain adaptability.

D1.justification: Table 3 and the experimental appendices retain the same hardware, framework, hyperparameters, preprocessing, and training-data information. Figure 6's revised caption repeats settings already documented in v1 Appendix A.7; no new reproducibility or resource-access information is supplied.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations and bibliography entries for HIVA, CF-VLM, OSC, and GAM-Agent. These are limited additions to the existing introduction and related-work discussion; the positioning narrative and novelty claims remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes limited wording and heading edits, standardizes SAS terminology, adds an affiliation and Acknowledgments, and repairs appendix figure references. The main narrative and section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 6 expands from one column to full width, and its incorrect TriviaQA noise-schedule caption is replaced with a description of the existing Arxiv SAS-weight study. Other tables and figures shift with pagination while retaining their contents and designs.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the existing evidence easier to identify and read: Figure 6 receives an accurate SAS-study caption and larger display, Appendix A.6 points to the correct Figure 5, and the abstract uses consistent SAS terminology. These resolve specific presentation defects, but the method, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and substantive limitations remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
